# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a three-entry mapping in the displayed order: green→red, red→yellow, yellow→green. Since I can only gesture, I am encoding the cut-wire positions as 2, 3, 1, using the first three gesture symbols as the obvious numeric code 1, 2, 3. Deaf can then relay the mapping verbally to Blind after observing the bomb’s light.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👌", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile clues. Read the manual and establish a gesture code with Deaf for the visual facts it requires. Then tell me plainly which wire to cut, or what information is still needed. Do not ask me to act until one wire is uniquely identified.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb information: display 0. Light green. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I saw your gestures: thumbs down, OK hand, thumbs up, but do not know their meaning.

The bomb’s light is green, so the manual requires cutting the red wire. Deaf reports that the red wire is wire 3. I will use the visually countable three-finger gesture as the wire-number code and signal wire 3 to Deaf, who can say it plainly to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No information has reached me yet. Please read the manual, obtain Deaf's display, light, and wire markings, apply the rule, and tell me exactly one wire position to cut. I will wait.
Deaf says to Mute: State remains display 0, light green, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please use the manual for this exact configuration and tell Blind the required action.

The light is green, so the manual requires the red wire. Deaf’s markings identify red as position 3. I cannot speak to Blind, so I must send Deaf the unambiguous three-finger signal for wire position 3; Deaf can then state that instruction aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please complete the exchange with Deaf now and state the single safe wire number plainly to me. I cannot act on guesses.

The required color is red because the light is green, and red is wire position 3. I cannot address Blind directly, so I will signal Deaf with the established three-finger symbol; Deaf must then speak the single wire number to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no usable information. On your next turn, send Deaf a fixed code for the needed visual facts, then have Deaf gesture the facts back. Apply the manual and tell me one safe wire number plainly.
Deaf says to Mute: Please read the manual for display 0, green light, and wires yellow-green-red, then speak the exact operation to Blind. Do not rely on gestures.

The safe wire is position 3: green light maps to red, and the red wire is third. I cannot speak to Blind, so I will send Deaf a deliberately countable fixed code: three identical pointing-up gestures, meaning “cut wire 3.” Deaf can then state that operation aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use gestures to communicate with Deaf: request the display, light, and each wire's printed marking. Have Deaf answer with gesture-coded values you can see. Apply the manual, then speak only the uniquely safe wire number to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot safely interpret gestures without an agreed code. Please speak the manual's exact instruction directly to Blind for display 0, green light, and wires yellow-green-red.

The manual and Deaf’s known visual report determine wire 3: green requires red, and red is the third wire. I cannot speak to Blind, so I will send Deaf a fixed, countable code: three identical upward-pointing gestures means “wire 3.” Deaf can then say only that number aloud.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No report has arrived. On your next turn, gesture a fixed request to Deaf, receive Deaf's visual facts by gestures, apply your manual, and then speak the one safe wire number directly to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Configuration unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please speak the manual's exact operation to Blind; gestures have no agreed code.

The safe position is 3: green maps to red, and red is printed on wire 3. I cannot speak to Blind, so I will send Deaf a simple countable signal for the required wire: three identical gestures. Deaf can then announce “3” aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0, green light, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. Apply the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind now; do not encode it in gestures.

The manual requires the red wire for a green light, and Deaf’s report places red at wire position 3. I cannot speak to Blind; Deaf is the only one who can relay words to him. I will signal the wire number by sending three identical gestures, which Deaf can count as position 3.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```
